resolutions.researcher_notes: Original ref (egyptoil-gas.com/reports/the-western-desert-egypts-giant-petroleum-reservoir/) is dead; replaced with the SAME report ('The Western Desert: Egypt's Giant Petroleum Reservoir', by Amina Hussien, Reham Gamal & Tasneem Madi), re-hosted as a PDF on egyptoil-gas.com's own site. Its 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert' table lists 'Shams-Obaiyed' as one of the Western Desert's 13 (then-)existing gas pipelines, with From=Shams, To=Obaiyed, Length=42 km, Diameter=18 in, Capacity=240 mmcf/d -- an exact match to this GEM entity, confirming operating status. Independently corroborated by Apache Egypt Companies' Feb. 2004 EIA (submitted to OPIC, hosted on miga.org -- a genuinely separate origin: company/regulatory filing vs. trade press): its route map places 'SHAMS' (inlet manifold) and 'Obayied' within the same Khalda/Matrouh-concession gas-gathering network feeding the operating 'Northern Gas Pipeline' (a.k.a. 'Western Desert Gas Pipeline'), and its text states gas 'is compressed, metered, and exported via the Western Desert Gas Pipeline.' Also cross-confirmed qualitatively (not cited, for context) by Egypt Oil & Gas's 2017 feature 'Phase III: Khalda Increases Gas Production at Hydra Field', which describes 'the pipeline that runs from the Shams manifold to Obayied gas plant' as active infrastructure. No contradictions found; nothing suggests the line is shut in. NOTE: both proposed refs are PDFs with compressed/deflate-encoded text streams, so the automated url_verifier substring screen (which reads raw response bytes) cannot find 'Obaiyed'/'Shams' in them and would report a false 'value not found' -- both HTTP 200s were confirmed live, and the table/route content above was confirmed manually via `pdftotext` extraction on the downloaded PDFs (the documented compressed-PDF false-negative pattern per url_verifier.py's own docstring).

StartLocation=Shams / EndLocation=Obaiyed confirmed directly: the egyptoil-gas.com 'Western Desert' report's pipeline table has a 'Shams-Obaiyed' row with From=Shams, To=Obaiyed (see Status [ref] note for the exact figures). Independently, Apache Egypt Companies' Feb. 2004 EIA (miga.org, a separate company/regulatory origin) places 'SHAMS' (an inlet gas manifold/train) and 'Obayied' on the same Western Desert route map, within the Khalda/Matrouh-concession complex, and states its 34-in 'Northern Gas Pipeline' handles gas exported from the 'Khalda concession, Martouh concession, Ras Kanayis concession, Ras El Hekma concession, Umbarka & South Umbarka concession' -- i.e. the same Matrouh-area concession cluster the GEM row's StartState/Province and EndState/Province ('Matruh') point to. StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=Egypt is trivially confirmed by both (both describe Egyptian Western Desert operations only). For additional context (not cited as a primary ref): Egypt Oil & Gas's 2017 Hydra-field feature explicitly names 'the pipeline that runs from the Shams manifold to Obayied gas plant', and a Shell/oilegypt.com history page places the Obaiyed field '35 km southwest of Matruh', both consistent with the Matruh attribution. No contradictions found. Same PDF-text-extraction caveat as the Status ref applies to the url_verifier automated screen on these two PDF URLs -- confirmed manually via `pdftotext`.
